protocol.scope: Retrospective 24-hour trajectory atlas with locked preservation diagnostics; no mortality-prediction modelling.
protocol.selection: Unlabelled target validation only. Outcome labels are not used to fit or select transport. Test results never change choices.
protocol.imputation: Existing independently trained, training-only SAITS recipes are retained. This is adaptation with access to target training data, not zero-shot transfer. Method weights are conservative design choices, not calibrated uncertainty.
protocol.clinical: OT cannot identify technical versus biological variation from these data alone. Preservation probes and support gates are empirical safeguards, not proof of biological invariance.
protocol.missingness: Hourly point/block removal measures sensitivity to lost hourly evidence; it does not simulate changes in raw-event density and hourly extrema. Missingness can encode illness and treatment.
protocol.eicu: Main documented-infection proxy and its timing remain unchanged. Strict culture flags describe a sensitivity subgroup; existing tensors remain anchored to the main proxy onset.
protocol.identity: Patient splits are inherited within databases. No reliable cross-version person linkage is available for MIMIC-III versus MIMIC-IV; cross-database person independence is not established. eICU patient holdout does not establish unseen-hospital generalization.
protocol.coverage: All clinical patients remain in metadata. Patients without sufficient observed shared cells/features have unavailable representations; unsupported eligible targets retain original embeddings. No cohort rows are deleted.
protocol.acceptance: Validation gates choose identity when correction is unsupported or fails preservation/stability criteria. Test results never switch the choice. QC PASS establishes implementation and provenance, not a claim that OT improves outcomes.
